as_told.title: Geological paper on hydrocarbon seepages under Giza

plain: The claim is that under the Giza Plateau, where the pyramids stand, there is a karst system, a network of caves and tunnels dissolved out of the rock, and that it sends hydrogen sulfide gas up to the surface. The researcher Geoffrey Drumm makes this point on two episodes (his name is also given as Jeffrey Drum), each time summarising a scientific paper. In the first he says the paper shows "a karst cave and tunnel system" that is "the source of hydrogen sulfide gas coming up from the Giza Plateau." In the second he reads out the paper's full title: "The development of sulfuric acid speleogenetic deposits within cavernous Middle Eocene beds and inference on hydrocarbon gas seepages, Giza Pyramids Plateau, Egypt." Speleogenetic means cave-forming. The title itself speaks of acid-formed cave deposits and gas seeping up through the plateau, which fits his reading. Whether the gas served any purpose for the pyramids, the title neither says nor rules out. Drumm brings it in to support his idea, set out in episodes about an energy grid and the true purpose of the pyramids, that the gas under Giza is part of what the pyramids were built to use.
